chain.label: Free-floating elevator design with no gust lock and undetectable jam
chain.trigger: the elevators (which, by design, did not have gust locks) were exposed to high, gusting surface wind conditions

chain.label: Ground gust criteria assume static 65-kt horizontal gust; not exceeded, so no inspection required
chain.trigger: the ground gust criteria specified in the regulation may not adequately ensure that critical flight control systems are protected from hazards introduced by ground gusts that contain dynamic, vertical wind components

chain.label: High gusting westerly surface wind during 2 days parked on ramp
chain.trigger: the airplane had been parked on the ramp at YIP for 2 days near a large hangar... exposed to high, gusting surface wind conditions

chain.label: Airplane parked immediately downwind of a large (0.25-mile) hangar
chain.trigger: a ramp area east of a large (about 0.25-mile long) hangar

chain.label: Hangar-generated localized turbulence with vertical components over the tail
chain.trigger: a small-scale horizontal gust of 58+ kts moved over the airplane... related to turbulence generated downwind of the hangar

caused_by.evidence: shortly after a 55 kt gust from 261° was introduced (consistent with the maximum ASOS-observed gust)
the airflow at the airplane's parked location was affected by the presence of the large hangar that generated localized turbulence

chain.label: Elevator driven rapidly up and down, slamming dynamically against mechanical stops
chain.trigger: moved the elevator surfaces rapidly up and down, which resulted in impacts against the elevator mechanical stops, imposing dynamic loads sufficient to jam the right elevator

caused_by.evidence: the airflow would provide a lifting motion followed by a downward push in less than 3 seconds... a hard slam of the elevators against either the upper or lower stop
When the airplane is parked, each elevator is free to move independently within the confines of the mechanical stops if acted upon by an external force, such as wind
an elevator under loading that dynamically impacts the stop is subjected to increased hinge moment (versus the static loading condition)

chain.label: Right elevator geared tab linkage locked overcenter, jamming elevator full trailing edge down
chain.trigger: the right elevator's geared tab's inboard actuating crank and links had moved beyond their normal range of travel and became locked overcenter, effectively jamming the right elevator in a full-TED position

caused_by.evidence: the effects of the large hangar near the accident airplane's parked location resulted in a turbulent windflow with vertical components that imposed dynamic loads on the elevator system sufficient to jam the right elevator

chain.label: Rotation speed increased about 5 kts for gusty wind, delaying the rotate call past V1
chain.trigger: we are going to delay our rotation because of the gusty, strong gusty winds

caused_by.evidence: the wind was "pretty gusty," so they agreed to increase the rotation speed about 5 kts

chain.label: Airplane did not respond in pitch and would not rotate despite full aft column input
chain.trigger: a large control column input was applied over the next 8 seconds... The airplane did not respond in pitch and did not rotate

caused_by.evidence: the right elevator's jammed condition rendered the airplane unable to rotate during takeoff

the flight crew's preflight inspection and control check during taxi... could not have detected the overcenter position of the right elevator geared tab's linkage or the resultant jammed elevator condition
it resulted in the check airman not calling "rotate" until 5 seconds after the airplane achieved V1

chain.label: High-speed rejected takeoff initiated 12 seconds after V1
chain.trigger: the captain executed the rejected takeoff 12 seconds after the airplane achieved V1 because he perceived that the airplane did not respond normally

caused_by.evidence: at 1452:05, the captain said, "hey, what's goin' on?" and, 3 seconds later, "abort"... "it wasn't flying"

chain.label: Airplane overran departure end of runway 23L at about 100 kts
chain.trigger: the airplane was traveling about 100 kts when it exited the paved surface off the departure end of runway 23L

caused_by.evidence: to successfully stop the airplane on the runway, the crew would have had to start braking once the airplane was about 5,000 ft into the takeoff roll. (The accident crew began braking about 5,800 ft into the roll.)

chain.label: Struck airport perimeter fence and raised road; landing gear collapsed, substantial damage
chain.trigger: traveled about 950 ft across the grassy part of the runway safety area before striking the airport perimeter fence and a raised, paved road before coming to a stop

caused_by.evidence: The nose landing gear and both main landing gear were bent, fractured, and displaced aft... damage was consistent with ground impact after the collapse of the landing gear

chain.label: 1R slide valve release cable incorrectly installed in the inflation valve assembly
chain.trigger: the cable had been installed incorrectly in the valve assembly, which prevented proper inflation

chain.label: 1R door evacuation slide failed to inflate, rendering the exit unusable
chain.trigger: when she pulled the manual inflation handle for the slide, it did not inflate... She blocked the unusable exit and redirected passengers

caused_by.evidence: the incorrect installation of the valve release cable in the valve assembly resulted in the failure of the 1R door evacuation slide to inflate

chain.label: One passenger sustained a minor injury during the evacuation
chain.trigger: All 110 passengers and 6 crewmembers evacuated the airplane with one reported minor injury (a leg laceration that required sutures)

caused_by.evidence: The 110 passengers and 6 flight crewmembers evacuated the airplane via emergency escape slides... One passenger received a minor injury
